topic: The Mathematical Foundations of Bitcoin: Trust through Cryptography
target_audience: University students with a basic understanding of algebra and computer logic.

sections.title: The Digital Fingerprint: Hash Functions (1 min)
lecture_lines: Hash functions take input to fixed-length strings.
They are one-way streets, impossible to reverse.
Changing input triggers the avalanche effect.

sections.title: Digital Signatures: Asymmetric Cryptography (1.5 min)
lecture_lines: Public-Key Infrastructure uses a key pair system.
Private key signs, public key verifies.
Math allows verification without revealing the secret.

sections.title: Proof of Work: The Mathematical Lottery (1.5 min)
lecture_lines: Miners race to find a random nonce.
The hash must start with specific zeros.
Success is instantly verifiable by the network.

sections.title: The Immutable Chain: Blockchain Integration (1 min)
lecture_lines: Blocks link via the previous block's hash.
Altering one block invalidates the entire chain.
This ensures security through mathematical immutability.
